headline: Profit turns positive on AMVUTTRA surge, though eases q/q
summary_short: Q2 revenue climbed 67% y/y to $1,291M and net income swung to a $164M profit from a $72M loss a year ago, even as net income and diluted EPS ($1.21) each slipped about 20% versus Q1 on higher R&D and SG&A spending.
summary_long: Net product revenue rose 74% y/y to $1,172M as AMVUTTRA grew 106% to $1,012M on higher U.S. ATTR-CM demand, partly offset by a shrinking ONPATTRO base; GIVLAARI and OXLUMO also grew. Royalty revenue rose 79% on higher Novartis Leqvio sales, while collaboration revenue fell 23% as the Regeneron research term wound down. Cost of goods sold rose to 25.4% of product revenue (from 21.1%) on AMVUTTRA's higher blended royalty rate. R&D rose 28% on Phase 3 trial costs for zilebesiran and nucresiran; SG&A rose 8% on AMVUTTRA launch marketing. Cash and equivalents reached $1,708M. No quantified forward guidance was disclosed in the filing.

drivers.explanation: Revenue and profit growth was driven by AMVUTTRA's continued ATTR-CM launch and higher Leqvio royalty revenue from Novartis, partly offset by lower Regeneron collaboration revenue and higher R&D and SG&A spending on late-stage trials and the AMVUTTRA launch.
Net product revenue growth was driven by AMVUTTRA demand from ATTR-CM patients in the U.S., plus growth in GIVLAARI and OXLUMO patients, partially offset by fewer ONPATTRO patients.
Cost of goods sold rose as a percentage of product revenue mainly due to higher AMVUTTRA sales and an associated increase in AMVUTTRA's blended royalty rate.
Cash increased primarily due to stronger operating cash flow from higher product-revenue collections, partially offset by increased capital expenditures and marketable-securities purchase timing.
